title: Rhythm Club, Amsterdam Club and Edmond Hall's Lafayette booking
summary: Scott keeps in touch with musicians and gets a show booking at the Lafayette.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I felt good about it. And then, right away I went up to the musicians club. And (inaudible) had opened up the Rhythm Club around 32nd Street. You heard about that.
Well, that's (inaudible). I had two places to go, the Rhythm Club was nearer, and then around 130th Street was the Amsterdam. So, you see, I kept in contact with the musicians.

Well, I go around there to the Rhythm Club and I come back home, and there'd be another -- on the telephone pad there, so-and-so called up, it'd say, call them up. So-and-so called, and I'd give my sisters tips to take the calls for me. I'd give them a little money.
Well, I went around there because I was lonesome in the house. I didn't have any men to talk to. My father used to -- man, he went to work and he came home and he ate his
dinner and read the newspaper and went to bed, and he did -- that was his routine. And my brother was too small to be of any comfort to me. I had to associate with other men, fellows, see.

And that's the reason I went around and talked to the fellows. We all spoke the same language, and I went around there and they'd say, hey, did you hear, so-and-so was in town. Who? And they'd name some new musician. Where's he playing at? Well, I heard he's playing at such-and-such a place. Well, that'll circle around and everybody would go up there to hear him, to see how good he was.

That's the way it was. So I went around, and I had to pass by the Lafayette in order to get to the Rhythm Club. And Edmond Hall came walking out. And -- hello, Scottie, hey, what are you doing? I say, I'm going down to the Rhythm Club. Say, what you doing? You're with Duke, aren't you? I just left Duke. I said, well, I'm not with him right now. He said, listen, book -- I want you next week.

I'm glad I met you. They knew I could play shows. They knew I could play shows. Because I had a lot of experience. So I went in there and played a show because I wanted to circulate, and from the show I did at Lafayette right there, right around the corner was the Rhythm Club, then I'd go down to 107 W. on 30th Street, and that was the Amsterdam.
So I was in between. I kept in contact with all the
musicians. Then I went back home, because, see, when you played the shows -- then I could play other jobs, get a gig in between. And still play the show.

And, do you know, I went home and I passed by the telephone and looked, and there was -- I forget now who it was, twas a big, anyhow. Now, how did they know that I wasn't with Duke? I didn't tell them. News gets around, it got around s in those days. Anything you did, anybody else in the music world -- musicians would know about it the next day.
